intended_object: The homomorphism that embeds the rank-four split maximal (weight) torus 𝔾_m^4 over 𝔽₂ into the short-root type-F₄ carrier, i.e. into the closed subgroup scheme of GL₂₆/𝔽₂ generated by the reduced root subgroups and the torus. On points, t is sent to diag(∏_j t_j^{w_i(j)}), where w_i runs over the 26 weights of V(ϖ₄): the 24 short roots and 0 counted twice. I took this from the docstring, the module documentation, and the companion `rootSubgroup` definition.
explanation:
The carrier `groupScheme` is the generated subgroup scheme `generatedGroupScheme 26 generator`. At index `.inr ()`, `generator` is the weight-torus coordinate map `weightTorusBaseChangeCoordinateMap ℤ (ZMod 2) f4ShortRootWeight`. That map restricts to the diagonal torus of GL₂₆ and then pulls back along the character map given by the F₄ short-root weight table `f4ShortRootWeight`. This table lists the 26 weights of the 26-dimensional representation; its first entry is ϖ₄ and it contains two zero weights.

`weightTorus` is the factorization of this generator through the carrier (`generatorToGeneratedGroupScheme ... (.inr ())`), precomposed with the `eqToHom` that identifies the split torus with Spec of its character-group Hopf algebra. The lemma `weightTorus_comp_carrierι` confirms that composing with the inclusion into GL₂₆ gives back the weight-torus morphism. So the definition is exactly the inclusion of the weight torus into the carrier, as its docstring says.

It is a specific object: one particular torus in one particular group scheme over 𝔽₂. The whole module is about the companion carrier over the prime field, so working over `ZMod 2` is part of what the object is, not an unnecessary restriction. Mathlib has no F₄ carrier or comparable torus embedding.
